subject: FRE
label: Grade 05
task: Meet the outcome of every unit in Grade 05 French, and keep one piece of evidence for each.
condition: A 36-week school year, 4 units, a teacher or guide, a learning book or device, and local examples in the local language first with English support.
standard: Each unit: at least 4 of 5 attempts correct, said or written, with one real example from home or school. Course pass: no unit at 'Not yet' after one retry, and a pass in SA1 and SA2.

modules.title: Describing my school
modules.intro: In this unit you work on 'Describing my school', taught in a way that is short, playful, with objects, pictures and talk. The target is clear: describe my school. You move from seeing it, to saying it, to doing it alone.
points: Listen first: your teacher or a recording says the new words or sentences from 'Describing my school' twice. You repeat them aloud.
Notice the pattern: find where the new sound, word form or sentence rule appears in a short text and mark it.
Use it: describe my school, first with help, then alone.
Check and fix: read your work aloud once more; fix one thing you hear is wrong.
modules.example: Solved: 'Mon ecole est grande. J'ai un cartable et une trousse. J'etudie les maths et l'anglais.' Swap in your own words. Method: Model run for 'Describing my school'. Teacher text (3 lines about a daily activity). Step 1, read it aloud together. Step 2, mark every word or sentence that uses the new pattern. Step 3, a learner writes or says two new lines of their own that use the same pattern. Step 4, the learner reads them aloud and corrects one slip. What a good answer looks like: the pattern is used correctly in both lines, the lines make sense, and the learner can say which part is the pattern.
modules.activity: About 20 to 30 minutes of class work, then one short practice task for home. Keep evidence: one page in your learning book.
modules.standard: Describe my school: at least 4 of 5 attempts correct, said or written, with one real example from home or school.
steps: Step 1, Describe the buildings. Mon école est grande et propre. [My school is big and clean.] Il y a vingt salles de classe, une cour, une bibliothèque et une cantine. [There are twenty classrooms, a yard, a library and a canteen.] Use il y a for there is and there are.

Step 2, Describe your class. Ma classe est lumineuse. [My class is bright.] Il y a vingt-cinq élèves. [There are twenty-five pupils.] Ma maîtresse est gentille. [My teacher is kind.] Notice maîtresse is feminine, so the adjective gentille ends with e.

Step 3, Say what you do and like. Ma matière préférée, c'est les maths. [My favourite subject is maths.] Je mange à la cantine. [I eat at the canteen.] À la récréation, je joue dans la cour. [At break I play in the yard.] Ask your partner the same.

Step 4, Dialogue. Sam : Comment est ton école ? [What is your school like?] Zoé : Elle est grande, avec une belle bibliothèque. [It is big with a lovely library.] Sam : Tu aimes ta classe ? [Do you like your class?] Zoé : Oui, j'adore ma classe ! [Yes, I love my class!]
Step 5, Fix errors. A child says Il y a vingt élève. Correction: Il y a vingt élèves, because the noun is plural. Another says ma école; use mon école, because mon is used before a vowel sound.

Step 6, Your turn: write four sentences about your school. Model answer: Mon école est petite mais jolie. Il y a douze classes et une grande cour. Ma matière préférée, c'est l'anglais. Je suis très content. [My school is small but pretty. There are twelve classes and a big yard. My favourite subject is English. I am very happy.]

modules.title: Regular verbs: er, ir, re
modules.intro: In this unit you work on 'Regular verbs: er, ir, re', taught in a way that is short, playful, with objects, pictures and talk. The target is clear: conjugate regular verbs. You move from seeing it, to saying it, to doing it alone.
points: Listen first: your teacher or a recording says the new words or sentences from 'Regular verbs: er, ir, re' twice. You repeat them aloud.
Notice the pattern: find where the new sound, word form or sentence rule appears in a short text and mark it.
Use it: conjugate regular verbs, first with help, then alone.
Check and fix: read your work aloud once more; fix one thing you hear is wrong.
modules.example: Solved: parler: je parle, tu parles, il parle, nous parlons, vous parlez, ils parlent. Method: Model run for 'Regular verbs: er, ir, re'. Teacher text (3 lines about a daily activity). Step 1, read it aloud together. Step 2, mark every word or sentence that uses the new pattern. Step 3, a learner writes or says two new lines of their own that use the same pattern. Step 4, the learner reads them aloud and corrects one slip. What a good answer looks like: the pattern is used correctly in both lines, the lines make sense, and the learner can say which part is the pattern.
modules.activity: About 20 to 30 minutes of class work, then one short practice task for home. Keep evidence: one page in your learning book.
modules.standard: Conjugate regular verbs: at least 4 of 5 attempts correct, said or written, with one real example from home or school.
steps: Step 1, Verbs ending in er follow one pattern. parler [to speak]: je parle, tu parles, il parle, nous parlons, vous parlez, ils parlent. Replace er with the endings e, es, e, ons, ez, ent. Example: Nous parlons français. [We speak French.]

Step 2, Verbs in ir like finir follow another. je finis, tu finis, il finit, nous finissons, vous finissez, ils finissent. Example: Elle finit ses devoirs. [She finishes her homework.] Nous finissons à quatre heures. [We finish at four o'clock.]

Step 3, Verbs in re like vendre [to sell]: je vends, tu vends, il vend, nous vendons, vous vendez, ils vendent. Example: Il vend des fruits. [He sells fruit.] The il form has no ending, only the stem vend.

Step 4, Practise a mixed dialogue. Maman : Qu'est-ce que tu fais ? [What are you doing?] Léa : Je finis mon exercice. [I am finishing my exercise.] Maman : Tu parles de quoi ? [What are you talking about?] Léa : Je parle du voyage. [I am talking about the trip.]

Step 5, Fix errors. A child says nous parlez. Correction: nous parlons, because nous goes with ons. Another says je finit. Correction: je finis, because je takes s in the ir pattern. Also ils vend should be ils vendent.

Step 6, Your turn: conjugate habiter [to live] with je, nous and ils, then complete: Elles (finir) leur travail. Model answer: j'habite, nous habitons, ils habitent. Elles finissent leur travail. [I live, we live, they live. They finish their work.]

modules.title: Negation and articles
modules.intro: In this unit you work on 'Negation and articles', taught in a way that is short, playful, with objects, pictures and talk. The target is clear: use ne pas and articles. You move from seeing it, to saying it, to doing it alone.
points: Listen first: your teacher or a recording says the new words or sentences from 'Negation and articles' twice. You repeat them aloud.
Notice the pattern: find where the new sound, word form or sentence rule appears in a short text and mark it.
Use it: use ne pas and articles, first with help, then alone.
Check and fix: read your work aloud once more; fix one thing you hear is wrong.
modules.example: Solved: 'Je ne parle pas arabe.' 'Il n'a pas de livre.' Ne goes before the verb, pas after it. Method: Model run for 'Negation and articles'. Teacher text (3 lines about a daily activity). Step 1, read it aloud together. Step 2, mark every word or sentence that uses the new pattern. Step 3, a learner writes or says two new lines of their own that use the same pattern. Step 4, the learner reads them aloud and corrects one slip. What a good answer looks like: the pattern is used correctly in both lines, the lines make sense, and the learner can say which part is the pattern.
modules.activity: About 20 to 30 minutes of class work, then one short practice task for home. Keep evidence: one page in your learning book.
modules.standard: Use ne pas and articles: at least 4 of 5 attempts correct, said or written, with one real example from home or school.
steps: Step 1, To make a sentence negative put ne before the verb and pas after it. Je parle anglais. [I speak English.] Je ne parle pas anglais. [I do not speak English.] Before a vowel ne becomes n': Il n'aime pas le lait. [He does not like milk.]

Step 2, Learn definite and indefinite articles. le, la, l', les [the]; un, une, des [a, some]. Example: J'ai un chat et des poissons. [I have a cat and some fish.] Le chat est noir. [The cat is black.] Choose le for masculine, la for feminine.

Step 3, Learn partitive articles. du, de la, de l' [some], used for things you cannot count: Je mange du pain. [I eat some bread.] Je bois de l'eau. [I drink some water.] Elle mange de la soupe. [She eats some soup.]

Step 4, After a negative, un, une, des, du, de la change to de or d'. Je n'ai pas de frère. [I do not have a brother.] Je ne mange pas de pain. [I do not eat bread.] Il n'a pas d'amis. [He does not have friends.]

Step 5, Fix errors. A child says Je mange pas de viande. Correction: Je ne mange pas de viande, because ne is needed. Another says Je n'ai pas des amis. Correction: Je n'ai pas d'amis. A third says Je ne bois pas du lait; say pas de lait.

Step 6, Your turn: make these negative: Elle a un vélo. Nous buvons du thé. J'aime les carottes. Model answer: Elle n'a pas de vélo. Nous ne buvons pas de thé. Je n'aime pas les carottes. [She has no bike. We do not drink tea. I do not like carrots.]

modules.title: Nationalities and character
modules.intro: In this unit you work on 'Nationalities and character', taught in a way that is short, playful, with objects, pictures and talk. The target is clear: describe people. You move from seeing it, to saying it, to doing it alone.
points: Listen first: your teacher or a recording says the new words or sentences from 'Nationalities and character' twice. You repeat them aloud.
Notice the pattern: find where the new sound, word form or sentence rule appears in a short text and mark it.
Use it: describe people, first with help, then alone.
Check and fix: read your work aloud once more; fix one thing you hear is wrong.
modules.example: Solved: 'Il s'appelle Karim. Il a dix ans. Il est egyptien. Il aime le football.' Method: Model run for 'Nationalities and character'. Teacher text (3 lines about a daily activity). Step 1, read it aloud together. Step 2, mark every word or sentence that uses the new pattern. Step 3, a learner writes or says two new lines of their own that use the same pattern. Step 4, the learner reads them aloud and corrects one slip. What a good answer looks like: the pattern is used correctly in both lines, the lines make sense, and the learner can say which part is the pattern.
modules.activity: About 20 to 30 minutes of class work, then one short practice task for home. Keep evidence: one page in your learning book.
modules.standard: Describe people: at least 4 of 5 attempts correct, said or written, with one real example from home or school.
steps: Step 1, Learn nationalities with masculine and feminine. français, française [French]; italien, italienne [Italian]; indien, indienne [Indian]; marocain, marocaine [Moroccan]; anglais, anglaise [English]; espagnol, espagnole [Spanish]. They begin with a small letter.

Step 2, Say who you are. Je suis marocain. [I am Moroccan, a boy.] Je suis marocaine. [A girl.] Maria est italienne. [Maria is Italian.] Ils sont indiens. [They are Indian.] Elles sont françaises. [They are French, all girls.]

Step 3, Learn character adjectives. gentil, gentille [kind]; drôle [funny]; timide [shy]; courageux, courageuse [brave]; généreux, généreuse [generous]; sérieux, sérieuse [serious]. The ending eux changes to euse for a girl.

Step 4, Describe people. Maria est italienne. Elle est courageuse et généreuse. [Maria is Italian. She is brave and generous.] Karim est marocain. Il est timide mais drôle. [Karim is Moroccan. He is shy but funny.] Add parce que for a reason.

Step 5, Fix errors. A child says Elle est courageux. Correction: Elle est courageuse. Another says Il est indienne. Correction: Il est indien. A third writes Français with a capital; as an adjective it is français.

Step 6, Your turn: describe an Indian girl who is kind and serious. Model answer: Priya est indienne. Elle est gentille et sérieuse. Elle est aussi très drôle avec ses amis. [Priya is Indian. She is kind and serious. She is also very funny with her friends.]

When do the formative checks FA1 to FA4 and the summative checks SA1 and SA2 happen?
FA1 to FA4 around weeks 6, 12, 24 and 30; SA1 in week 18; SA2 in week 36.

What evidence do you keep for each unit, and why?
One page in your learning book. It shows what you can really do and lets a teacher check it against the standard.
ladder: L1: say and read familiar words and short sentences.
L2: read short texts and write connected sentences.
L3: write paragraphs and speak on a topic with notes.
L4: write for different purposes and analyse how texts persuade.
L5: write and argue at length; handle unseen texts.
L6 (degree): academic reading, writing and citation.
L7 (postgraduate): publish, teach or translate with expert accuracy.
